definition.def: If there is some prospect of something happening, there is a possibility that it will happen.
examples: Unfortunately, there is little prospect of seeing these big questions answered. [+ of]
The prospects for peace in the country's eight-year civil war are becoming brighter. [+ for]
There is a real prospect that the bill will be defeated in parliament.

definition.def: A particular prospect is something that you expect or know is going to happen.
examples: They now face the prospect of having to wear a cycling helmet by law. [+ of]
After supper he'd put his feet up and read. It was a pleasant prospect.

definition.def: Someone's prospects are their chances of being successful, especially in their career.
examples: I chose to work abroad to improve my career prospects.
...a detailed review of the company's prospects.

definition.def: When people prospect for oil, gold, or some other valuable substance, they look for it in the ground or under the sea.
examples: He had prospected for minerals everywhere from the Gobi Desert to the Transvaal. [VERB + for]
In fact, the oil companies are already prospecting not far from here. [VERB]

examples.sentence: In business as a whole, there are a number of factors encouraging the prospect of greater equality in the workforce.
The morning was dull and damp, and Bingham also seems to have been less than keen on the prospect of climbing the hill.
Others, though, are fascinated by the prospect that a computer might create something as original and subtle as our best artists.
Although he never liked the prospect of a business career, he stayed with it to please his family.
While the prospect of bringing extinct animals back to life might capture imaginations, it is, of course, far easier to try to save an existing species which is merely threatened with extinction.
Salespeople like Schaefer walk the line between the common practice of buying a prospect's time with a free meal, and bribing doctors to prescribe their drugs.
The technology raises the prospect of Britain becoming self-sufficient in renewable energy and drastically reducing its carbon dioxide emissions.
The prospect has certainly been wrenched much closer to the realm of possibility now that a major physical hurdle - the speed of light - has been cleared.
Any prospect of the elm returning relies heavily on trees being either resistant to, or tolerant of, the disease.

Of course, poachers will eventually become aware of the prospect of fake eggs among the real ones - especially when customers try to bite into an egg and break their teeth on the GPS transmitter instead.
